beats.intro: Chapter fifty-one. [[sub]]To multiply polynomials, every term in one must multiply every term in the other.
beats.mono: Start with a monomial times a binomial: x squared, times x cubed plus seven y. [[dist]]The distributive property sends x squared to each term inside. [[box]]An area model shows the same thing: a rectangle x squared tall, split into two parts across. [[c1]]x squared times x cubed is x to the fifth. [[c2]]x squared times seven y is seven x squared y. [[ans]]Add the parts: x to the fifth plus seven x squared y. They aren't like terms, so that's the final answer.
beats.binom: Now two binomials: x plus nine, times x plus seven. [[rect]]Picture a rectangle x plus nine wide and x plus seven tall. [[split]]Split each side into its two terms, and the rectangle splits into four parts. [[c1]]x times x is x squared. [[c2]]x times nine is nine x. [[c3]]Seven times x is seven x. [[c4]]Seven times nine is sixty-three. [[like]]The two x strips are like terms: seven x plus nine x is sixteen x. [[ans]]So the product is x squared plus sixteen x plus sixty-three.
beats.foil: For two binomials, the four products have names. [[f]]First: the first terms, a times c. [[o]]Outer: the outside terms, a times d. [[i]]Inner: the inside terms, b times c. [[l]]Last: b times d. [[word]]That's the FOIL method, first, outer, inner, last. [[same]]It finds exactly the four cells of the area model, so it's the distributive property in a fixed order.
beats.neg: Watch the signs. [[q]]Multiply two x minus three, times x plus five. [[cells]]Treat minus three as negative three in its own column. [[c1]]Two x times x is two x squared, [[c2]]two x times five is ten x, [[c3]]negative three times x is negative three x, [[c4]]and negative three times five is negative fifteen. [[like]]Combine the like terms: ten x minus three x is seven x. [[ans]]The product is two x squared plus seven x minus fifteen.
beats.big: Longer polynomials work the same way, with a bigger grid. [[q]]x plus two, times x squared plus three x minus one: [[grid]]two rows and three columns make six products. [[fill]]Fill every cell. [[diag]]Like terms line up along the diagonals: three x squared and two x squared, then negative x and six x. [[ans]]The product is x cubed plus five x squared plus five x minus two.
beats.q3: Quick check. Fill in the grid.
beats.div: To divide a polynomial by a monomial, divide every term by the monomial. [[q]]Take a to the tenth b to the fourth, minus a to the eighth b to the fifth, divided by a squared b cubed. [[split]]Split it into two fractions, one for each term. [[t1]]a to the ten minus two, b to the four minus three: a to the eighth b. [[t2]]a to the eight minus two, b to the five minus three: a to the sixth b squared. [[ans]]The quotient is a to the eighth b, minus a to the sixth b squared.
beats.q4: Quick check. Divide by the monomial.
beats.wrap: To sum up. [[w1]]To multiply polynomials, multiply every term of one by every term of the other. An area grid keeps track. [[w2]]For two binomials, FOIL lists the four products: first, outer, inner, last. [[w3]]Then combine like terms. [[w4]]To divide by a monomial, divide each term separately. [[end]]Now try the chapter practice.
beats.final3: Last one. Divide by the monomial.
beats.finish: Great job. That's the end of chapter fifty-one, and of unit nine.
